comparator.name: Aardwetenschappen (Earth Sciences)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 programme-specific regulations explicitly cover entrants from 2023 through 2026. The major comprises 135 EC, including 75 required EC, and the degree leaves 45 EC of profiling space. The example uses the first-listed surface-formation route, with four 7.5 EC level-two courses, two 7.5 EC advanced taught choices and a compatible two-part 15 EC fieldwork sequence. The current route page lists Data Analysis and Statistics first and is used for that tie-break. The 15 EC thesis follows the current GEO3-1323 requirements. A link from the student route page points to the legacy GEO3-1324 course, whose different entry rules apply to pre-2023 entrants. The 2026 OER governs this example.

alternatives.concept: Study how rocks, soils, water, climate and life interact to shape the Earth’s surface. Combine geology, geochemistry, Earth observation and modelling with coastal and delta studies. Evolution and ecology add perspectives on life through time, while resource and energy assessment and governance address how people use and change Earth systems.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Earth Sciences bachelor. Utrecht lists four equally formal specialisations and does not identify one as the general route. Vorming van het aardoppervlak appears first in the current official curriculum, so it is selected by neutral official order independently of UCR fit. Within that route, official order also resolves the published choices.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One strong 24-course Earth-systems programme is feasible. The only generator-eligible direction outside the core is the formal educational minor, but UCR lacks subject didactics, supervised school practice and teacher qualification. Water, climate and hazards are already major organising strands of the closest curriculum; splitting them off would largely reshuffle the same environmental-science courses rather than produce a genuinely different programme.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study Earth systems, minerals, rocks, geological history and geophysical processes. Utrecht develops identification and field mapping through its required fieldwork sequence.
Both examine chemical equilibria, minerals and water-rock interactions; Utrecht also supplies a broader chemistry and isotope-geology foundation.
Both address the subsurface and its use; Utrecht reconstructs Dutch stratigraphy and geological development, while UCR focuses on contemporary resources and storage.
Utrecht's dedicated geomorphology course has no single UCR course counterpart.
Utrecht's compulsory 15-EC geological fieldwork sequence remains unmatched by one ordinary UCR course.
Both study life through time. UCR focuses on evolutionary mechanisms and phylogeny, while Utrecht also examines the interactions between life and the geological environment.
Both analyse coastal and river processes in relation to floods and land use; UCR emphasises nature-based engineering applications.
Both use GIS and remotely sensed Earth data for spatial environmental analysis.
Both examine groundwater and surface-water processes; UCR combines aquifer mapping with soils and resource applications.
Both study delta evolution, subsidence and water dynamics; UCR emphasises present-day adaptation and management.
Utrecht's route-specific source-to-sink field module has no ordinary UCR course equivalent.
Utrecht's route-specific lowland-genesis field module has no ordinary UCR course equivalent.
Both develop computational work with scientific data; Utrecht additionally teaches the physics of internal and surface Earth processes.
Both provide calculus and mathematical foundations; Utrecht integrates introductory statistics and Earth-science applications.
Both develop statistical analysis for scientific data; UCR adds probability theory and simulation.
Both develop research questions and evidence-based reporting. UCR uses a team project with a regional sustainability partner, while Utrecht requires an individual Earth Sciences thesis.
The genuine 45-EC elective, minor or study-abroad space remains open and is not assigned invented Earth Sciences content.

notes.text: UCR covers Earth systems, geological history, minerals and rocks, soils, water, geochemistry, GIS and quantitative methods. Utrecht’s route develops these subjects through dedicated geomorphology, delta and coastal dynamics and a longer required geological fieldwork sequence. Its 15 EC thesis is an individual research project. UCR’s partner project is team-based and its topic depends on the available sustainability brief.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht Earth Sciences studies how the Earth changes through interactions among rocks, water, climate and life. A broad first year leads to one of four specialisations. This example follows Vorming van het aardoppervlak, which focuses on the processes that form and change landscapes.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines Earth science with water, climate, ecology and quantitative environmental research. It includes geological study and field and laboratory work. Utrecht’s selected route adds dedicated geomorphology, delta and coastal dynamics, a longer geological fieldwork sequence and an individual 15 EC thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The example selects Data Analysis and Statistics, Delta Evolution and Subsurface, Coastal and River Dynamics, and the Italy fieldwork modules. It preserves 45 EC of profiling space.

componentNotes.es-y1-fieldwork: Entry requires at least 22.5 EC of first-year major courses from periods one and two, completed before 1 March.
componentNotes.es-y2-data-statistics: The example selects Data Analysis and Statistics, the first option on the current route page. Entry requires first-year mathematics and statistics.
componentNotes.es-y2-delta: Selected as the first of two advanced taught choices. Entry requires 45 EC of first-year major courses and 7.5 EC of level-two major courses.
componentNotes.es-y2-coastal-river: Selected as the second advanced taught choice. Entry requires 45 EC of first-year major courses and 7.5 EC of level-two major courses.
componentNotes.es-y2-fieldwork-source-sink: Entry requires 75 EC in the major before 1 March, including Fieldwork 1 and 15 EC of relevant level-two courses.
componentNotes.es-y2-fieldwork-lowland: This example uses the lowland-genesis module, taken with the Source to Sink fieldwork module.
componentNotes.es-y3-thesis: For the current programme, entry requires all first-year courses and at least 7.5 EC of advanced route study other than Fieldwork 2. The thesis is written in English with a Dutch summary.
componentNotes.es-y3-elective-space: 45 EC of profiling study remain open. Approval, level, overlap and other degree requirements apply.
